methods.description:
List your webhooks.

Each summary has the status, format, URL, last delivery and last success, and the circuit breaker state (`circuitFailures`, `circuitOpenedAt`).

Get one webhook's full configuration.

Adds the triggers, the receiver's auth (redacted to header names and whether a secret is set), the retry and timeout limits, `lastError`, and a `warning` when this instance's trigger evaluator is not running.

methods.summary: Create a webhook that POSTs chain events to your URL.
methods.description:
Create a webhook that POSTs chain events to your URL.

Takes a `name`, a `url`, and `triggers` built with `trigger.*`; each trigger is validated before anything is provisioned, and an invalid one is a 400. The signing secret comes back once in `signingSecret`, so store it. A webhook starts at the chain tip and never backfills: use `replay` for history. Hosted accounts cap `maxRetries` at 7 and `timeoutMs` at 30000.

methods.summary: Change a webhook's name, URL, format, auth, or delivery limits.
methods.description:
Change a webhook's name, URL, format, auth, or delivery limits.

Send only the fields to change: `name`, `url`, `format`, `authConfig`, `maxRetries`, `timeoutMs`, `concurrency`. Triggers are not part of an update. Resolves to the updated webhook.

methods.summary: Stop deliveries without deleting the webhook.
methods.description:
Stop deliveries without deleting the webhook.

Resolves to the updated webhook. `resume` turns it back on.

methods.summary: Start delivering again after a pause.
methods.description:
Start delivering again after a pause.

Also clears a circuit-breaker pause, which happens after 20 straight failed deliveries. Resolves to the updated webhook.

Delete a webhook.

Resolves to `{ ok: true }`. Throws a 404 when the webhook does not exist.

Issue a new signing secret.

The new secret comes back once in `signingSecret`. Update the receiver that calls `verifyWebhookSignature` with it: deliveries are signed with the new secret from now on.

methods.summary: Send a one-off test delivery to a webhook's URL.
methods.description:
Send a one-off test delivery to a webhook's URL.

Built for the webhook's format and SSRF-guarded. Logged as a delivery
row, visible via `deliveries`.

methods.summary: The last 100 delivery attempts, newest first.
methods.description:
The last 100 delivery attempts, newest first. The server caps the
result; there is nothing to page. Pass `window` (ISO timestamps, at most
31 days wide) to read only the attempts dispatched in `[from, to)`, for
example one hour of the heat strip; `total` then counts that window.

methods.summary: Get a webhook's hourly delivery counts for the last 7 days.
methods.description:
Get a webhook's hourly delivery counts for the last 7 days.

Each hour has delivered, waiting, and gave-up counts, plus the current
queue depth, failed attempts per hour, and the usual band. Pass
`{ days: 30 }` to also get 30 daily totals. This is the events chart on
the detail page.

methods.summary: Get one delivery attempt with its payload and response.
methods.description:
Get one delivery attempt with its payload and response.

Includes the outbox context (payload, response headers). This is the
delivery card on the detail page.

methods.summary: Re-deliver historical events over an existing webhook.
methods.description:
Re-deliver historical events over an existing webhook.

Pass `fromBlock` and `toBlock`; the range is capped at 100,000 blocks. A replay is historical only and never moves the live cursor. It is idempotent: the same range twice is a no-op, so pass any string as `force` to re-deliver it. Replays carry `is_replay` and use the standard `chain.{type}.apply` envelope. Resolves to `replayId`, `enqueuedCount`, and `scannedCount`. A second replay while one is running is a 409. `sbtc_withdrawal_swept_confirmed` is forward-only and never replayed. Hosted accounts get 5 replays an hour.

params.name: range
params.type: { fromBlock: number; toBlock: number; force?: string }

methods.summary: List the events a webhook gave up delivering.
methods.description:
List the events a webhook gave up delivering.

Returns up to 100 dead-lettered events, newest failure first. Each row's `id` is what `requeue` takes.

methods.summary: Push one dead-lettered event back onto the delivery queue.
methods.description:
Push one dead-lettered event back onto the delivery queue. `outboxId` is
the `id` of a row from `dead`.

Null for test deliveries and events already compacted out of the
outbox.

fields.description:
ISO timestamp of the delivered event's block. `null` for test
deliveries, events already compacted out of the outbox, and rows
written before this column existed.

Null for test deliveries and events already compacted out of the
outbox.

The row's position within its block/tx, from the outbox's `row_pk`.

types.summary: The fields of a webhook you can change.

types.name: WebhookActivity
types.summary: A week of hourly delivery counts and what is waiting now.

fields.name: hours
fields.description: 168 hours, oldest first.

fields.name: waiting
fields.description: Pending rows right now, no time bound.

fields.name: byEventType
fields.description:
7-day counts per `event_type` (same 168-hour window as `hours`), e.g.
`chain.stx_transfer.apply` — the config card's per-trigger volume.

fields.name: usualByHourOfDay
fields.description:
Typical delivered attempts for each UTC hour of day (p10 and p90 of the
last 28 days, from `webhook_deliveries`). Null at low volume, where
"usual" is not meaningful.

fields.name: days
fields.description:
Present with `?days=30`: 30 UTC days, oldest first, from
`webhook_deliveries` (2xx is delivered, everything else failed).

types.name: WebhookActivityDay
types.summary: One UTC day of delivery attempts (`GET /:id/activity?days=30`).

fields.name: day
fields.description: YYYY-MM-DD, UTC.

types.name: WebhookActivityHour
types.summary: One hour of `webhook_outbox` activity (`GET /:id/activity`), zero-filled so the events chart always has 168 bars.

fields.name: hour
fields.description: ISO timestamp, UTC hour start.

fields.name: failed
fields.description:
Failed attempts in the hour (no response or non-2xx), from
`webhook_deliveries`. Attempts, not events: a retried-then-delivered
event counts here but is `delivered` above.

types.name: WebhookAuth
types.summary: What a webhook's receiver credentials look like once redacted for a response — never the bearer token, basic-auth string, or header values themselves, only enough to show what's set.

fields.name: headerNames
fields.description: Keys of any extra headers the receiver expects — never their values.

fields.name: hasSecret
fields.description: True when a bearer token or basic-auth string is set, whatever it is.

types.name: WebhookDeliveryDetail
types.summary: One delivery attempt with its outbox context.

fields.name: outboxStatus
fields.description:
The outbox row's own status — `null` once it's gone (compacted after
delivery, or never had one, e.g. a test delivery). Only `"dead"` means
a resend is possible: it's the one status `POST /:id/dead/:outboxId/
requeue` accepts.

fields.name: eventIndex
fields.description:
The row's position within its block/tx, from the outbox's `row_pk`
(`event_index` for a chain-trigger row). Null when `row_pk` carries
none — a settlement or reorg outbox row, or no outbox row at all.

types.name: WebhookDetail
types.summary: A webhook with its triggers, auth, retry, and timeout settings.

fields.name: triggers
fields.description: Chain-trigger filters.

fields.name: receiverCertExpiresAt
fields.description:
When the receiver's TLS certificate expires, from the periodic probe.
Null for http receivers, refused or unreachable hosts, and webhooks not
probed yet.

fields.name: warning
fields.description:
Set when this instance's chain-trigger
evaluator isn't running (`SUBGRAPH_SOURCE` != `streams-index`) — the
webhook will never fire until that's fixed. Null otherwise. Surfaced
on create (so it's seen immediately) and on every read (so `secondlayer
webhooks doctor` reports it for a webhook created before the mismatch,
or on an instance whose config changed since).

circuitFailures

Consecutive failed deliveries (reset to 0 on a success). On the
summary so the list can show a failing receiver per row without a
per-row fetch.

Owning product, derived from the name prefix (`MANAGED_NAME_PREFIXES`).
When non-null the API refuses to rename the webhook.
